user.title: Connect via USB / Serial
user.description: Select one USB or serial port. Opening this form does not touch any port; only the selected port is opened, and only after you confirm the next step.

verify.title: Verify Monoprice amplifier
verify.description: Verify the Monoprice amplifier connected to {port}. Only this port is opened; the amplifier is asked for its zone 11 status while the baud rate is detected, and the port is closed again before you continue.

data.all_on_volume: Volume to set when a master zone is switched on (0 to leave alone)
data.auto_link_speed: Let the integration work up to it automatically

data_description.baud_rate:
The amplifier always powers on at 9600 baud, so this is the speed to work up to, not the one the connection starts at. A higher speed lowers command latency but is less tolerant of long or noisy RS-232 runs.

Leave the checkbox on unless you have a reason not to. The integration then raises the speed one step at a time, confirming each, remembers the highest that worked on your cabling, and never retries one that failed. Turned off, it switches straight to the speed you picked: if the wiring cannot carry it the amplifier still changes speed on receipt and becomes unreachable until you remove its power for 30 seconds.

zone_names.title: Name each zone's media player
zone_names.description: Optional. A blank field keeps that zone's default "Zone N" name; the amplifier itself has no way to store a room name, so this lives only in Home Assistant and can be changed later from Reconfigure or this integration's Configure option.
